**UNO – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 1 000 points (or play all your own cards). Points come from opponents’ remaining cards when you finish a round. | | **Deck** | Standard UNO set has 108 cards:
• Four colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 each
• Each color contains one “0” and two copies of numbers 1–9.
• Eight action cards per color:
  • +2
  • Skip
  • Reverse

• Six Wild cards: four *Wild* + two *Draw‑Four*. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the whole deck.
• Deal seven cards face down to each player.
• Place the rest as a draw pile; flip the top card onto an open discard pile. If it’s an action or wild, treat it like a normal start (see below). | --- ### Gameplay Loop Players take turns clockwise around the table. #### On Your Turn 1. **Match & Play** - You may lay down one card if its rank or suit matches either the top card on the discard pile OR if it's a Wild card. - A *Wild Draw‑Four* can only be played if you have no other legal move (you’re forced to show proof otherwise). 2. **If You Can’t Match** - Draw one card from the draw pile. - If this new card is playable, you may immediately place it. Otherwise, keep it and end your turn. 3. **Action Cards** - `Skip`: Next player loses their turn. - `Reverse`: Order of play reverses direction (two players → same effect as Skip). - `+2`: Next player draws two cards AND misses their turn. - `Wild`: Player chooses next colour. - `Wild Draw‑Four`: Same as Wild but forces next player to draw four cards unless they challenge successfully. 4. **Ending a Round** When you play your last card: - Say “UNO!” before the next person starts playing. Failure to say “UNO!” results in drawing two penalty cards. - Score points equal to the sum of values of opponent's remaining cards: - Numbered cards: Face value - Action cards (`+2`, `Skip`, `Reverse`): 20 pts - Wild / Wild Draw‑Four: 50 pts 5. **Winning** First player to reach 1 000 total points wins the match. For casual games, stop after a single round or at a lower target. --- ### Extra Tips & Variations | Variation | How It Works | |-----------|-------------| | **Stacking (+2/+4)** | Players may stack multiple +2 or +4 cards instead of drawing. Opponent then needs to collect them all or use another +2/4. | | **No Challenge Rule** | Some groups allow Wild Draw‑Four without requiring a challenge check. | | **House Rules** | Many families add custom actions such as “Swap hands,” “Shuffle everyone’s hand,” etc. Just agree beforehand! | Enjoy the colorful chaos—remember, the key is quick thinking and keeping track of those “UNO!” calls!
